aria: Animated recap of the Heat's 114 to 108 road win at Sacramento: Giannis Antetokounmpo's jumper with 59.1 seconds left, quarter-by-quarter scoring, his 29 points and 14 rebounds, the top scorers, how the Heat won, and the next game at Utah.
notes: Box score from the Heat's 114–108 win over the Sacramento Kings in Sacramento on Nov 8, 2026, from the Covers.com box score, with game details from the AP (via Yahoo Sports), Field Level Media, FortyEightMinutes, Roundtable, The Kings Herald, Yardbarker and the Land of Basketball daily summary. All 114 Heat points and all 108 Kings points are accounted for in the box score. The quarter scores are Covers' and match Field Level Media's running scores (34–30, 68–59 at the half, 91–81 after three). The 16-point Heat lead is from Covers, the AP and Yardbarker; Sacramento's 5-point lead is Covers'. Team totals (threes, assists, fast-break points, field goals, free throws) are Covers'. The Jazz's record is from the site's standings; the road record (3–3) is Yardbarker's; the next game, Sacramento's 0–5 home record and Sabonis's absence are from the AP and Field Level Media.

The play of the game is an original illustration of Giannis Antetokounmpo's jumper with 59.1 seconds left that put Miami up 112–105 (Field Level Media; FortyEightMinutes has the same score with under a minute left). He went 0 for 1 from three, so it was a two, from 110–105. Sacramento had tied it at 95 on De'Andre Hunter's free throws with 6:12 left before Miami closed on a 19–13 run (AP). The recaps don't describe how he got the shot, so it is drawn as a plain pull-up. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Miami Heat or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Antetokounmpo’s listed 6-foot-11 and 250 pounds (Basketball-Reference), with arms scaled to a reported 7-foot-3 wingspan (Heating Up), in the Heat's road red with No. 7 (Eurohoops). It is an original silhouette with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
